entities.summary: Electronic music, a genre primarily employing electronic musical instruments, digital instruments, and circuitry-based music technology, has its roots in early 20th-century avant-garde movements. This sonic phenomenon emerged in the 1920s, with pioneers like Thelonious Monk and Edgard Varèse experimenting with electronic instruments to expand the sonic palette. The development of tape loops, synthesizers, and other electronic equipment further transformed the music landscape in the 1950s and 1960s, paving the way for the emergence of popular electronic music genres like techno, house, and trance. As a global phenomenon, electronic music has become a staple of contemporary popular culture, with its influence extending to fashion, visual art, and dance. The genre's ability to adapt and evolve has allowed it to transcend geographical boundaries, making it a truly global entity. With its rich history and diverse range of sub-genres, electronic music continues to captivate audiences and inspire new generations of artists. From its humble beginnings in experimental circles to its current status as a mainstream force, electronic music has left an indelible mark on the music world.
